b_records.quote: Proposition 2.I: Let F1(x; alpha, beta, theta) and G1(x; alpha, beta, theta) be the cdfs of the EPAD and EWD, each with parameters alpha, beta and theta. Then F1(x; alpha, beta, theta) <= G1(x; alpha, beta, theta). That is the EPAD(alpha, beta, theta) exhibits first-order stochastic dominance over the EWD(alpha, beta, theta). Proof: Certainly, if x < 0, F1(x, alpha, beta, theta) = 0 and G1(x, alpha, beta, theta) = 0. Thus, the inequality holds when x < 0. If x >= 0, 1 + theta x^beta >= 0 indicating that F1(x; alpha, beta, theta) = [1 - (1 + theta x^beta)e^{-theta x^beta}]^alpha <= G1(x; alpha, beta, theta) = [1 - e^{-theta x^beta}]^alpha. This completes the proof.
b_records.family: EPAD (Exponentiated Power Ailamujia distribution) F1(x) = [1 - (1 + theta x^beta)e^{-theta x^beta}]^alpha vs EWD (exponentiated Weibull distribution) G1(x) = [1 - e^{-theta x^beta}]^alpha, common parameters alpha, beta, theta

hypotheses.text: F1 and G1 have the same parameters alpha, beta, theta

conclusion.direction: F1(x) <= G1(x) for all x, i.e., the EPAD variable is larger than the EWD variable in the usual stochastic order (first-order stochastic dominance)

b_records.quantifiers: all x (x < 0 both cdfs are 0; x >= 0 the stated inequality)
b_records.ambiguity: The paper states the result as 'first-order stochastic dominance' of EPAD over EWD via F1 <= G1; under the usual convention X >=st Y iff F_X <= F_Y, this means EPAD >=st EWD. Printed as 'Proposition 2.I'.
